ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Caroline wants to write the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 in the square $4 \times 4$ in such a way that every row and every column has each number. You see how she started. What number must be put in the place of $x$?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The figure is a 4×4 grid. It can be directly seen: the first row is 1, blank, x, 2; the first column of the second row is 4, and the second column is 1; the second column of the third row is 3; the second column of the fourth row is 2. First look at the second column, which already has 1, 3, 2, so the second column of the first row can only be 4. method.method_draft: First read the image as a 4×4 grid: top row has 1 in column 1, x in column 3, and 2 in column 4; column 2 contains blank, 1, 3, 2 from top to bottom. From the text, use the rule that each column must contain 1, 2, 3, 4 exactly once. Since column 2 already has 1, 3, and 2, its top blank must be 4. Then use the row rule on the top row: it has 1, 4, x, 2, so the only missing number is 3. Therefore x must be 3.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the top row shows 1, blank, x, 2, while the second column shows blank, 1, 3, 2. From the text, every row and column must contain 1, 2, 3, 4. In the top row, because 1 and 2 are already present, the two remaining cells must be 3 and 4. Test the two possibilities for x. If x were 4, then the other blank in the top row, at column 2, would have to be 3; but column 2 already contains a 3 in the third row, violating the column rule. Therefore x cannot be 4, so x must be the other possible value, 3.
